A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and are readable throughout. The methods, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–I can be matched reliably; v3 inserts a NeurIPS checklist without removing scientific content.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation and real-robot experiments, including success rates, sampling ablations, hyperparameter sensitivity and low-data evaluations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the main success-rate comparisons and appendix experiments. Their retention still qualifies as reporting original results.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same proprioception-guided alignment cost, Unbalanced Optimal Transport objective, DTW-based sampling and joint behavior-cloning training. The policy architectures are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both retain the same six-task manipulation suite and its allocation across sim-to-sim and sim-to-real experiments. RGB and point-cloud observations, visual domain shifts, and reset, texture and shape OOD scenarios remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments. MMD remains in the simulation and low-data comparisons; real-world tables retain Source-only, Target-only and Co-training. The sampling ablation retains its no-sampler and oracle variants.

E3.justification: The Source/Target/Target-OOD partitions, demonstration counts, preprocessing, architectures and experimental settings are retained. Appendix C still specifies batch sizes of 256 and 128 and a co-training ratio of 0.9; checklist statements introduce no revised protocol.

E4.justification: The simulation-data scaling analysis, sampling ablation, hyperparameter sensitivity, scarce-target-data evaluation, transport-plan visualization and latent-space analyses are unchanged. Figures 4 and 9–11 and Appendices D–I contain the same evidence.

E5.justification: Checklist item 7 newly discloses and explains the absence of error bars, citing the effort required for real-world evaluation trials. This is a limited reporting addition: no uncertainty estimates, seeds, repeated-run counts or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: The numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged across the main text and appendices. For example, Tables 7 and 8 retain average real-world in-distribution success rates of 0.73 for image policies and 0.77 for point-cloud policies.

T1.justification: The problem assumptions, OT and UOT formulations, sampling equations and appendix mathematics are unchanged. Notational spacing edits do not revise mathematical content, and the checklist adds no theoretical result or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and scope: UOT-based sim-and-real co-training, temporally aligned sampling, generalization to scenarios seen only in simulation, and the claimed improvement of up to 30% in real-world success rate.

C2.justification: The new checklist explains that real-world evaluation effort makes producing error bars impractical, adding a specific qualification about the empirical evidence. Section 6 retains the existing limitations concerning visual gaps, quasi-static prehensile tasks and aligned real-world demonstrations.

D1.justification: v1 already links the project website for videos and analysis; v3 newly states in checklist item 5 that code and data are available there. It also identifies the authors as demonstration collectors. Implementation details remain unchanged, and the PDFs alone do not verify website availability.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds citations to X-Sim: Cross-Embodiment Learning via Real-to-Sim-to-Real and One-Shot Imitation Under Mismatched Execution, numbered 37 and 46 in v3. These extend attribution without changing the research positioning or adding evaluated baselines.

P1.justification: v3 inserts a standalone NeurIPS checklist before Appendix A, repeats the existing project link in the abstract, updates equal-contribution markings and makes small terminology and punctuation edits. The scientific narrative and appendix organization remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–11 and Tables 1–9 retain their content, captions and organization. Minor table-width changes accompany the Co-train. label edits, while front-matter reflow and the inserted checklist alter page layout. No scientific visualization is added or redrawn.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves documentation through explicit code/data-access information, acknowledgment of missing error bars and two additional related-work citations. The scientific evidence remains unchanged. The gain is limited: uncertainty estimates remain absent, and the checklist claims complete compute reporting without supplying GPU or runtime details.
